summary.title: Nim Days: Day 7 - Shorturl service
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small URL shortener in Nim using the Jester web framework and SQLite, with a home form, a POST endpoint that stores URLs, and a GET endpoint that redirects short IDs.
keywords: how to make a url shortener
takeaways: Jester provides a sinatra-like DSL for defining GET and POST routes in Nim.
SQLite via db_sqlite stores the mapping between a generated integer id and the long URL; the table is created on first run if missing.
A POST to /shorten parses the JSON body, reuses an existing id for a known URL or inserts a new row with tryInsertId, and returns the id as JSON.
A GET to /@Id looks up the stored URL and redirects, or returns 404 when the id is unknown.
summary.summary: This tutorial, part of the Nim Days series, builds a URL shortening service similar to bit.ly. It uses the Jester web framework for routing, asyncdispatch for async support, htmlgen and json for output, and db_sqlite for storage in /tmp/mytest.db. The page walks through a home page with a jQuery and fetch-based form, a /shorten POST endpoint that saves URLs and returns their ids, and a /@Id route that redirects to the stored URL. The code is shown inline and a full version is linked as a gist.
